originalText:
Certainly! Here is a polished version that ensures clarity.

In today’s fast-paced world, it is important to note that studies show the district programme drives meaningful impact. The team conducted an assessment of 17 facility reports in order to identify stock-outs. This comprehensive analysis provides a robust overview of the situation, highlighting the programme’s commitment to better outcomes.

In conclusion, the future isn’t coming. It’s already here.

findings.title: Assistant-style preface
findings.original: Certainly! Here is a polished version that ensures clarity.
findings.sentence: Certainly! Here is a polished version that ensures clarity.
findings.rationale: The sentence describes the assistant's action instead of belonging to the document.
findings.action: Delete the preface and begin with the deliverable.

findings.title: Unsupported quality assurance
findings.sentence: Here is a polished version that ensures clarity.
findings.rationale: The sentence asserts quality without naming the procedure or evidence that produced it.
findings.action: Name the validation, coverage, comparison, or test; otherwise delete the assurance.

findings.title: Generic world-setting opener
findings.sentence: In today’s fast-paced world, it is important to note that studies show the district programme drives meaningful impact.
findings.rationale: The opener supplies generic context that could introduce almost any subject.
findings.action: Begin with the specific problem, event, or decision.

findings.title: Interpretive metadiscourse
findings.original: it is important to note that
findings.sentence: In today’s fast-paced world, it is important to note that studies show the district programme drives meaningful impact.
findings.rationale: The author tells the reader how to weigh a point instead of showing the consequence or evidence. Ordinary explanatory glosses such as ‘in other words’ are not flagged without a semantic redundancy check.
findings.action: Delete it when the support is already clear; otherwise add the missing consequence or evidence.

findings.title: Vague attribution
findings.sentence: In today’s fast-paced world, it is important to note that studies show the district programme drives meaningful impact.
findings.rationale: The source is too vague for the reader to verify or weigh.
findings.action: Name and cite the source, or remove the attribution and narrow the claim.

findings.title: Vague impact claim
findings.sentence: In today’s fast-paced world, it is important to note that studies show the district programme drives meaningful impact.
findings.rationale: The phrase asserts impact without naming what changed, for whom, or by how much.
findings.action: Replace it with the measured outcome, mechanism, beneficiary, and time frame.

findings.title: Weak verb plus nominalisation
findings.sentence: The team conducted an assessment of 17 facility reports in order to identify stock-outs.
findings.rationale: A weak verb and abstract noun delay the action.
findings.action: Use the corresponding direct verb where grammar permits.

findings.title: Wordy filler
findings.sentence: The team conducted an assessment of 17 facility reports in order to identify stock-outs.
findings.rationale: The phrase uses more words than the idea requires.
findings.action: Replace it with the direct equivalent.

findings.title: Quality label without criterion
findings.sentence: This comprehensive analysis provides a robust overview of the situation, highlighting the programme’s commitment to better outcomes.
findings.rationale: The quality adjective is not tied to a named test, comparator, coverage rule or validation result.
findings.action: Replace the label with the procedure and result that support it.

findings.rationale: The sentence asserts quality without naming the procedure or evidence that produced it.
findings.action: Name the validation, coverage, comparison, or test; otherwise delete the assurance.

findings.action: Name the validation, coverage, comparison, or test; otherwise delete the assurance.

findings.title: Superficial participial analysis
findings.original: , highlighting the programme’s commitment to better outcomes
findings.sentence: This comprehensive analysis provides a robust overview of the situation, highlighting the programme’s commitment to better outcomes.
findings.rationale: The trailing clause often labels significance without establishing a mechanism or consequence.
findings.action: Replace it with the concrete consequence or delete it.

findings.title: Recap ending
findings.sentence: In conclusion, the future isn’t coming.
findings.rationale: A generic recap often repeats what the reader has just read.
findings.action: Delete the label and end on the final concrete implication, decision, or action.

findings.title: Fake-profound ending
findings.original: the future isn’t coming. It’s already here.
findings.sentence: the future isn’t coming. It’s already here.
findings.rationale: The final line substitutes a generic aphorism for a concrete ending.
findings.action: Delete it and end on the last specific fact, implication, or next action.

principles: Score editorial defects, not presumed authorship.
Treat meaning preservation as a hard gate, not a style preference.
Do not rewrite source-reported language as if it were the current author's claim.
